title: Don’t suppress women-led agitation against ropeway, VPP warns govt

ai.summary: The Voice of the People Party (VPP) warns the Meghalaya government against suppressing women-led protests against the Shillong Peak Ropeway Project, which residents fear threatens water sources. VPP president Ardent Miller Basaiawmoit says the government must respect public consent for development projects.

facts.claim: The Voice of the People Party (VPP) has warned the NPP-led MDA Government against attempting to suppress the women-led agitation against the proposed Shillong Peak Ropeway Project
facts.quote: The Voice of the People Party (VPP) has warned the NPP-led MDA Government against attempting to suppress the women-led agitation against the proposed Shillong Peak Ropeway Project

facts.claim: VPP president Ardent Miller Basaiawmoit said the party could no longer remain a silent spectator to the government’s indifferent attitude towards their demand for the immediate suspension of the project
facts.quote: VPP president Ardent Miller Basaiawmoit on Friday said the party could no longer remain a silent spectator to the government’s indifferent attitude towards their demand for the immediate suspension of the project

facts.claim: The women under the banner of the Joint Action Committee Against Shillong Ropeway Project took part in a public rally to press for its suspension
facts.quote: women under the banner of the Joint Action Committee Against Shillong Ropeway Project taking part in a public rally on Thursday to press for its suspension

facts.claim: Deputy Chief Minister Prestone Tynsong and South Shillong MLA and Cabinet Minister Sanbor Shullai have maintained that the project will not be scrapped
facts.quote: Deputy Chief Minister Prestone Tynsong and South Shillong MLA and Cabinet Minister Sanbor Shullai have maintained that the project will not be scrapped

ai.background_note: Women in Shillong are protesting against the Shillong Peak Ropeway Project due to concerns about water sources, with the VPP joining the movement to support their demands.
